gold: Wellens syndrome with critical left anterior descending coronary artery stenosis

selector.rationale: Variant Angina best explains the chest pain and ECG changes, particularly the deeply inverted T-waves and upright T-waves during pain, without ST segment elevation, which is more characteristic of variant angina than myocardial infarction.

rejected.label: Acute Coronary Syndrome
rejected.why: Lack of ST segment elevation and normal troponin levels

rejected.label: Hypertensive Heart Disease
rejected.why: No clear evidence of heart failure or significant left ventricular hypertrophy

rejected.label: Coronary Artery Disease
rejected.why: While present, it is a broader category and Variant Angina is a more specific diagnosis that explains the patient's symptoms
